To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the charge properties of the surface and pore wall of a polyethersufone membrane are modified by the adsorption of multilayer polycations/polyanions.
the zeta potential of the membrane surface can be controlled by the polyelectrolectrolytes used in the adsorption process and the concentration of the solutions.
the charge of the membrane surface is modified by the alternate adsorption of polycationic and polyanionic polyelectrolys and the charge of the pore walls can also be modified.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of multilayer polycation/polyanion systems adsorbed on polymeric membranes by streaming potential, membrane potential, and diffusion measurements.
the characterization of membranes functionalized with polyelectrolys by means of streaming potential measurements.
the development of new membrane materials by the use of polyelectrolectrolytes as modifiers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, by means of multilayer buildup, it is possible to modify both the charge properties of the pore walls and the surface properties of the membrane.

the tangential streaming potentials are a good tool to investigate the charge properties of the membrane outer surface, whereas the membrane potential measurements give information on the charge properties of pore walls.

the tangential streaming method is a very powerful tool to characterize the outer surface of a membrane modified by multilayers of polyelectrolys, while the membrane potential method can be used to characterize the pore walls of a membrane modified at the same time by multilayers and by a functionalization of the pore walls.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the multilayer PE adsorption on the PES membrane surface can be used to tailor the membrane charge properties and that this technique could be applied for the surface functionalization of membranes in order to improve their performance.

the zeta potential of the outer membrane surface is positive after multilayer adsorption of polyelectrolys at low concentration, whereas the zeta potential is negative after adsorption of polycation and polyanions at high concentration.
the multilayer PE films on a membrane surface have a significant influence on the charge and transport properties of the membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the charge properties of the outermost surface of the PES membrane are strongly dependent on the concentration of the polyelectrolys in the solution and on the number of bilayers deposited on the membrane.
the tangential streaming current technique is a very powerful tool to characterize the charge properties of the outermost layer of a membrane.
it is possible to control the charge of the pore walls of a membrane, which can be used to control the charge properties and the selectivity of the membrane.
